### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**4** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **60** of **216** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **156** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **156**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **101** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **10** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json d93acbbe552989632d22269e90841ed44860b589` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `c89c724212a785714731ceab00a47c1b54e77c0d` — the merge of head `cf1d52e814b9939010427c25fec3d601984ab0cf` into base `d93acbbe552989632d22269e90841ed44860b589`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin c89c724212a785714731ceab00a47c1b54e77c0d && git checkout c89c724212a785714731ceab00a47c1b54e77c0d
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin d93acbbe552989632d22269e90841ed44860b589 cf1d52e814b9939010427c25fec3d601984ab0cf && git checkout -B drift-repro d93acbbe552989632d22269e90841ed44860b589 && git merge --no-ff cf1d52e814b9939010427c25fec3d601984ab0cf

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json d93acbbe552989632d22269e90841ed44860b589
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `37f60fd639a0b16460ed0e80c62e73e09c0302a0`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/services/service-automation/src/builtin/crud-nodes.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/builtin/crud-filter-guard.test.ts + packages/spec/src/automation/flow-node-expression-paths.ts (`flowFilterOperands`, `isExpressionEnvelopeShaped`), packages/spec/src/data/filter-comparand-type.ts (`isAcceptedFilterComparand`), packages/spec/src/data/filter.zod.ts (`FieldOperatorsSchema`, `AST_OPERATOR_MAP`, `FILTER_OPERATORS`), packages/spec/src/data/filter-comparand-operators.ts (`LIST_COMPARAND_OPERATORS`), packages/services/service-automation/src/guard-refusal.ts (`refuseNode`), packages/services/service-automation/src/dag-traversal.ts (`evaluateValueEnvelope`), .changeset/29050-record-node-operand-value.md (read for ②)

Face: narrowing (`Clause-②: no (narrowing)` at the start of a line in the PR body and in the changeset). No published schema path and no governed path is in the file list. The floor is every path of the diff outside the prose faces: both files under `src/builtin/`. The cited code was read, not reviewed. Inputs: the claims 6577916318 and 6577943359, the os-dev-report 6579367914 (claims checked, not adopted), the PR body, the file list, the net diff `origin/main...37f60fd6` (3 files, +290/−6), and the check-runs on the head.

Check-runs on the head at 2026-11-02T14:24Z: 46 runs. 39 completed, every one `success` or `skipped`, none failed. 7 still running: Test Core (1/8) to (6/8) and Type Check · workspace. The gate verdict is not final until those complete; this record does not stand in for them.

PR author: `objectstack-fleet[bot]`; head and base in the same repository. No relay note is owed.

### ① Derived judgments

Each change the diff makes to an accept set or a public surface, named and judged.

1. `resolveNodeFilter` now judges every evaluated operand before it is written into the copied filter. An evaluated operand that is not a member of the spec's accepted comparand set (`isAcceptedFilterComparand`: string, number, bigint, boolean, `null`, `Date`) and is not a list is refused. **Right.** This is the rule the card states.
2. An evaluated list is accepted only when the operand's path ends in `$in`, `$nin` or `$between` and every member is a member of the accepted set. **Right.** The three are exactly the operators whose enforced slot takes an array on `main` (`FieldOperatorsSchema`; the spec's own `filter-comparand-shape.test.ts` pins the same three).
3. An evaluated list at any other position is refused: a field's implicit equality, a scalar operator's comparand, a list operator's single element (path ends in a number), an `$and`/`$or` member, an `$and`/`$or` value, and `$not`. **Right.**
4. The nothing guard keeps its message and is answered first when both classes occur in one filter. **Right.** The two refusals are one node result each; neither echoes the evaluated value.
5. The refusal is returned through `refuseNode`, so its `errorClass` is `guard`. **Right** (see ③ a).
6. An operand the author wrote as a literal is not judged: the loop skips every operand that is not envelope-shaped. The copied filter is changed only at operand paths. **Right.** Author-written fields, operators, `$and`/`$or`/`$not`, nested-relation conditions and query placeholders reach the engine as written.
7. `isAcceptedFilterComparand` becomes a runtime import from `@objectstack/spec/data`. **Right.** The barrel exports `./filter-comparand-type` on `main`; the package already imported a type from that subpath, so no new dependency edge is added.
8. `LIST_COMPARAND_OPERATORS` is a new local constant equal to the spec's unexported set. **Right for this head**, with a follow-up (③ c). The new test holds it equal to the schema's array-accepting operators by behaviour, so a fourth list operator in the grammar reds this package.
9. The `storedMetadataFilterRefusal` docblock now says an operand envelope evaluates to a value only, so the resolved filter names no column the authored one does not. **Right.** An evaluated object of any shape is refused at every position.
10. No export, type, signature or schema of `@objectstack/service-automation` or `@objectstack/spec` changes. `registerCrudNodes` is unchanged. No door that accepts written flow metadata changes. **Right.** The only narrowing is the run-time value a record node takes at a filter operand.
11. The refusal text and the changeset name the accepted set as "a string, number, boolean or date". The enforced set is the spec's six kinds: bigint passes at every operand position, and `null` passes as a member of an evaluated list at a list operator. **Wording narrower than enforcement.** Should-fix; see ④ finding 1.

### ② Semver level

- Changeset: `.changeset/29050-record-node-operand-value.md`, `'@objectstack/service-automation': patch`. The package is published (`18.2.0`, not private). **Level right.** AGENTS.md Post-Task Checklist step 3: `Metadata-protocol: none` takes `patch`; a non-protocol breaking change ships `patch` and keeps its BREAKING banner and its ADR-0087 disposition. Both are present.
- `Metadata-protocol: none`. **Right.** What a metadata author can write does not change: `flowFilterSlotSchema` on `main` is untouched, and the same flow definition is accepted by the save door, by lint and by `registerFlow` as before. What narrows is a run-time value.
- `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` at the start of a line in the PR body and in the changeset body, one spelling on both carriers. **Right.** The pm-dispatch rule: `yes` means the card widens an accept set or enlarges a public surface; a card that narrows a published accept set is `no`, and `(narrowing)` is the BREAKING arm. The dispatch claim's conditional `yes (narrowing)` does not stand; the dev's deviation to `no (narrowing)` is the correct spelling. This record is the isolated review that spelling owes.
- ADR-0087 marker: exactly one, `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`, with its reason: no key is added, removed, renamed or reshaped; no export or type changes; nothing for `objectstack migrate meta` to rewrite; no tombstone. **Right.** The changeset body also carries the one-line fix an upgrading author needs (make the expression evaluate to the compared value; write the condition in the filter).
- `Skills-docs: follow-up owed — content/docs/automation/flows.mdx, skills/objectstack-automation/SKILL.md` is in the PR body, as the `(narrowing)` arm requires. The seat files the owed card and rewrites the line to `follow-up #N` before ACCEPT (review-checklist). Not yet done at this head.
- Check Changeset check-run: `success`.

### ③ Boundary flags

(a) **Guard, not a routable fault.** Answer: the guard class holds. `refuseNode`'s two conditions are met: re-running the flow unchanged cannot succeed, because the expression at that operand reads a value of a kind the position never takes, and the fix is to the metadata (the expression, or the filter). The nothing guard in the same function is the precedent for a run-time-evaluated operand refused as a guard. A `fault` edge does not route it; a `try_catch` region still catches it, which the test pins at executor level. The dev's deviation from the dispatch delta's "flow fault" shape is accepted on this record; the seat notes it in its round report. Not escalated.

(b) **Who carries the docs and skill follow-up.** Answer: a separate card, filed by the seat. `skills/**` is a Tier H governed surface; folding the edit into this PR makes the whole PR Tier H on one path. The card's text states the rule only (ruling C), the same sentence the changeset carries. The seat rewrites `Skills-docs: follow-up owed — FILES` to `follow-up #N` before ACCEPT. Not escalated; it is the seat's own act.

(c) **List-operator set local or in spec.** Answer: local on this head, because the dispatch's file surface excludes `packages/spec/**` and the behavioural reconciliation test holds the two sets equal. The spec's stated reason for keeping `LIST_COMPARAND_OPERATORS` out of the `data` barrel is "no reader"; this PR is a reader, so the reason no longer holds. Escalated to the seat as a should-fix follow-up card: export the split (or a predicate over it) from `@objectstack/spec/data` and have the executor read it, retiring the local copy and the behavioural reconciliation in favour of a reference.

(d) **Scope boundary.** One boundary question beyond this rule is handled under ruling C. It is not part of this PR.

### ④ Design judgment

**Does the rule hold at every operand position?** Yes, against the tree. `flowFilterOperands` on `main` yields a path for every envelope in a filter: a field's value, each operator-map entry, each element of an authored list, a nested-relation field's value, an `$and`/`$or` member that is an envelope, an `$and`/`$or` value that is not a list, and `$not`. `operandValueRefusal` judges by the value and by the path's last segment only. A non-list, non-accepted value is refused everywhere. A list is accepted only when the last segment is `$in`, `$nin` or `$between` and every member is accepted; a numeric last segment, a field name, a scalar operator, `$and`, `$or` and `$not` refuse a list. The new tests pin eleven positions on `delete_record`, the object case on all three nodes, and the guard class at executor level. All three record nodes resolve their filter through the one function; `create_record` has no filter.

**Are legitimate literals and author-written structure unchanged?** Yes. Only envelope-shaped operands are judged. The copy is written only at operand paths. `copyFilter` shares class instances, so an evaluated `Date` reaches the engine as the same object; the CEL engine represents temporal values as `Date`, so a computed date passes. Number `0`, `false` and the empty string pass: membership is by type. A literal object, a literal list, an authored `$`-keyed structure and a query placeholder are handed on as written.

**Is the local list-operator set complete against the grammar on `main`?** Yes. `FieldOperatorsSchema` declares 17 operators; the ones whose enforced slot accepts an array are `$in`, `$nin` and `$between`, and the spec's own tests pin that set. `$contains` is declared with a string comparand. `AST_OPERATOR_MAP` lowers to no further list operator, and `FILTER_OPERATORS` adds none. `$between` is a pair: the guard accepts a list of any length of accepted members there, and the engine's own range door judges the length. That is a value question, not a structure question, and it stays the engine's.

**Findings, each a rule gap, each graded.** No must-fix.

1. **Should-fix.** The declared accepted set and the enforced accepted set differ in wording. The refusal text and the changeset name four kinds; the code accepts the spec's six. In particular a `null` member of an evaluated list at a list operator is not refused by this guard; the engine's set-membership door refuses it later as a routable failure, not as a guard. Either refuse a `null` list member here, as the nothing guard refuses a `null` operand, or name the enforced set in the message and the changeset. Behaviour is not wrong; the declaration is narrower than the code.
2. **Should-fix.** The list-operator set is a second copy of a spec constant that spec keeps unexported for a reason that no longer holds. Follow-up spec card (③ c).
3. **Boundary, not a finding of this rule.** Handled under ruling C (③ d).

Nothing in the cited code contradicts the change. The narrowing takes no declared capability away at the consumer: no door accepted an evaluated object or list at an operand as a declared capability; the spec ledger on `main` already names an operand a value slot. The change makes the spec's own description real at run time.

## Contract review

Delta review over the record on `37f60fd639a0b16460ed0e80c62e73e09c0302a0`, by the same reviewer. The new head is one commit on that head (`cf1d52e8`, 3 files, +29/−19), landing that record's should-fix 1 and nothing else. Every judgment of the earlier record that the delta does not touch stands. Face: narrowing (`Clause-②: no (narrowing)` at the start of a line in the PR body and in the changeset); no published schema path and no governed path in the file list. Inputs: the diff `37f60fd6..cf1d52e8`, the PR body and file list at the new head, the dev's round-2 report 6580952142 (claims checked, not adopted), and the check-runs on the new head. Check-runs on `cf1d52e8` at 2026-11-02T15:26Z: 52 runs, all completed; 37 `success`, 15 `skipped`, none failed, none running. The PR's head is `cf1d52e8`.

### ① Derived judgments

1. An evaluated list at an `$in`, `$nin` or `$between` comparand is now refused when an entry is `null`, with the same guard and the same refusal as any other non-value entry (`a list whose entry [i] is nothing`). **Right.** The member check is `member === null || !isAcceptedFilterComparand(member)`; an `undefined` entry was already refused and is now worded `nothing` too.
2. The check runs only where a list is accepted at all: a list at any other position is still refused whole, before the members are read. So the null-entry rule holds at every list position by construction. **Right.**
3. A literal list the author wrote is untouched: the loop judges envelope-shaped operands only, as before; an authored list and its entries reach the engine as written, for the engine's own doors to judge. **Right.**
4. `kindOfOperand` now words `null` and `undefined` as `nothing` first. A top-level `null` or `undefined` operand never reaches it (the nothing guard answers first, unchanged). **Right.**
5. The refusal text names the set as "string, number, bigint, boolean or date, or a list of them with no empty entry at an `$in` / `$nin` / `$between` comparand". The enforced set at a scalar position is `isAcceptedFilterComparand` less `null` (the nothing guard owns `null`); at a list position it is a list of the same, less `null` entries. **The declaration now equals the enforcement.** The function docblock states the same split in the same words.
6. The changeset's "A value" and "Refused" bullets name the same set and the empty-entry refusal. **Right.**
7. Nothing else moved. The diff touches the two docblocks, the refusal text, the member predicate, `kindOfOperand`, one test fixture entry and one test row, and two changeset bullets. No export, type, signature, schema or door changes; the three record nodes still resolve their filter through the one function.
8. The PR body's `Skills-docs:` line now reads `follow-up #29418 — content/docs/automation/flows.mdx, skills/objectstack-automation/SKILL.md`; #29418 is open and rule-only in its title. The list-operator export follow-up is #29419, open. **Right**; both are the earlier record's ③ (b) and ③ (c) answers carried out.

### ② Semver level

Unchanged from the earlier record, re-read on the new head. `'@objectstack/service-automation': patch`; `Metadata-protocol: none` (no door that accepts written flow metadata changes; the narrowing is a run-time value); `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` at the start of a line on both carriers, one spelling; exactly one ADR-0087 marker, `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`, with its reason; the BREAKING banner and the one-line fix are present. The round-2 edit changes two prose bullets of the changeset body and no declaration line. **Still right.** Check Changeset check-run: `success`.

### ③ Boundary flags

(a) Guard class: unchanged and still right. The empty-entry refusal is a guard, as the nothing guard beside it is; a `fault` edge does not route it, a `try_catch` region catches it. The dev chose the not-a-value refusal's message over the nothing guard's; the message names the node, the expression, the place and the entry index, and echoes no value. Accepted.

(b) Docs and skill follow-up: carried out as a separate card, #29418. The `Skills-docs:` line is rewritten to `follow-up #29418`. Nothing further owed on this head.

(c) List-operator set: carried out as a separate spec card, #29419. The local set stays on this head, held equal to the grammar by the behavioural reconciliation test. Nothing further owed on this head.

(d) Handled under ruling C.

### ④ Design judgment

The delta is judged over the floor of the earlier record; the position coverage, the untouched author structure and the completeness of the list-operator set stand as judged there, since no line of that logic moved.

**Does the null-entry refusal hold at every list position?** Yes. A list is accepted only when the operand's path ends in `$in`, `$nin` or `$between`; only there are entries read, and every entry is held to the accepted set less `null`. A list anywhere else is refused whole. A `null` scalar operand is the nothing guard's, answered first. So no evaluated `null` reaches the engine from any operand position, alone or inside a list.

**Does it leave literal lists untouched?** Yes. Only envelope-shaped operands are evaluated and judged; an authored list is copied and handed on as written, and the engine's set-membership and range doors keep judging it.

**Do the text, docblocks and changeset name exactly the enforced set?** Yes. All three name five scalar kinds and a list of them with no empty entry at the three list operators; the code enforces the spec's six-kind set less `null` at a scalar position and the same per entry at a list position. The function docblock says why `null` is absent from the named set (the nothing guard owns it). No wording is wider or narrower than the code.

**Did anything else move?** No. The test gains one fixture entry and one refusal row; the new pin is the only behavioural assertion added, and it is red with the member check removed per the dev's ablation claim, which is consistent with the diff (the `member === null` arm is the only new predicate).

Findings: none. Should-fix 1 of the earlier record is closed. Should-fix 2 is carried by #29419, outside this PR by design. No must-fix.

## 维护者速读

- 改了什么:flow 的记录节点(get/update/delete_record)把过滤条件里算出来的操作数当作值，不当作查询算子。值只能是字符串、数字、bigint、布尔或日期；在 `$in`/`$nin`/`$between` 处可以是这些值的列表(不能有空项)。其他一律在查询前按守卫拒绝。
- 为什么改：规则 C 下的安全后续(#29050)。规则写在 changeset 里，此处不展开。
- 风险与回滚：收窄(BREAKING,patch)。作者写的过滤结构和字面量不变。算出对象或列表放进单值位置的 flow 会在该节点失败。回滚即 revert。
- 先看:`packages/services/service-automation/src/builtin/crud-nodes.ts` 的 `resolveNodeFilter` / `operandValueRefusal`。

## 席位核对

**ACCEPT** · `domain:server` seat 5 · `os-steve` · `session_01ADHkmQKwKFCp1m6Pb6Q8c1` · 2026-11-02T15:28Z · head `cf1d52e814` · Refs #29050 (second follow-up under ruling C, claim 6577943359)

1. **Shape:** draft against `main`, `Refs #29050`, with no closing keyword. A **patch** changeset for `@objectstack/service-automation` with a BREAKING banner and the ADR-0087 marker `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`. `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`, `Metadata-protocol: none`, `Skills-docs: follow-up #29418`. Not governed: 306 changed lines, 3 files.
2. **Against the order:** the rule in the changeset is implemented at every operand position the three record nodes resolve, through one function. Confirmed by the at-tier contract review: round 1 PASS, round 2 delta PASS on this head.

Each new pin goes red with its check removed. Check-runs on this head: all completed, none failed, Lint & Repo Gates and TypeScript Type Check green.
5. **Out of scope:** #29418 (skills/docs) and #29419 (spec export of the list-operator split). One further boundary is handled under ruling C.
